description: Held-out pastes for the map lane at /analyze, written on 2026-09-29 after the scorer was tuned on pastes.json and run once, untuned, to check that the tuning generalises. Same schema as pastes.json: `expected` = right answers (empty = no map should be named), `related` = near siblings that are fair to show but are not the answer. The 40 cases from hold-m4a-dinner on were added on 2026-10-06 from the r9 live review (pastes sent to the live /api/analyze), before the round-9 matcher changes; 29 have a map, 11 do not.

cases.text: Living next to a nuclear plant gives you less radiation than eating a banana a day. Meanwhile coal plants kill thousands every year through air pollution and nobody marches against them.

A: Why is everyone suddenly excited about mini reactors? B: Because they can be built in a factory and shipped, so you don't get the Hinkley Point overruns. A: Every design so far has come in more expensive per kilowatt than the big ones.
I'm a translator. Two years ago I had more work than I could handle, now agencies send me machine output to 'post-edit' at a third of the rate. Don't tell me AI isn't taking jobs.
If the only thing that matters in an AI economy is who owns the compute, then workers have no bargaining power left. Either we spread ownership of capital or we get neo-feudalism.

Finland's basic income trial gave 2,000 unemployed people 560 euros a month with no conditions. They did not work much more than the control group, but they reported being happier and less stressed. Supporters called it a success; critics said it proved nothing about employment.

A: Sending more weapons to Israel right now makes America complicit in what's happening in Gaza. B: Israel has a right to defend itself, and cutting aid mid-war rewards Hamas. A: Nobody said cut it all, attach conditions like we do with every other country.
A: Walls work, look at the drop in crossings in the sectors where it was built. B: Most fentanyl comes through legal ports of entry, in cars driven by US citizens. A wall does nothing about that.

A new analysis of census data finds that wages for native-born workers without a high school diploma grew more slowly in metro areas that received the largest inflows of immigrant labor during the 2010s, though the effect disappears for workers with some college.
Global warming is a hoax pushed by grant-hungry scientists. Temperatures were higher in the 1930s.

A: We can't hit net zero without pulling carbon out of the air. B: Carbon capture has failed at almost every coal plant that tried it, it's just a license to keep burning. A: Cement and steel have no other option.

Berlin froze rents in 2020, and within a year the number of apartments advertised for rent had fallen by half while prices in the uncapped market jumped. The constitutional court threw the law out anyway.
Raising the minimum wage just gets people replaced by kiosks.
A: My kid's anxiety got way better once we took Instagram away. B: That's one kid. The big studies find tiny effects of screen time on wellbeing.
We made a pact with the other parents in our class that nobody gets a smartphone before 14. Flip phones only. It only works if everyone does it.
A: A robotaxi dragged a pedestrian in San Francisco and Cruise got shut down. These things aren't ready. B: Human drivers kill 40,000 Americans a year. One awful incident doesn't beat that record.
Mandating vaccines for schoolchildren is government overreach.
A: My town voted to stop fluoridating the water. B: Calgary did that and cavities in kids went up, so they put it back.
Cultivated meat is never going to be as cheap as chicken. The bioreactors are tiny and the growth medium costs a fortune.
Every other rich country has universal background checks and a fraction of our gun deaths. Thoughts and prayers aren't a policy.
States with the death penalty don't have lower murder rates than states without it. If it deterred anyone, you'd see it in the numbers.
Tax billionaires' wealth, not just their income.
Forgiving student loans is a handout to future doctors and lawyers, paid for by people who never went to college.
Remote work is here to stay. Office occupancy in big cities is still stuck around half of what it was in 2019, and the companies forcing people back are losing their best staff.
The SEC treating every token like a security just pushes crypto companies offshore. After FTX, though, pretending the industry can police itself is a joke.
If a civilization can run ancestor simulations, simulated minds would outnumber real ones, so odds are we're in one.
Psilocybin therapy got people out of depression that nothing else touched, in the trial I read about. The FDA rejecting MDMA therapy was a disaster.
Working four days for the same pay sounds great until you're a nurse or a teacher. It only works for office jobs.
Puberty blockers for kids are an experiment. The Cass Review found the evidence was weak, and several European countries have pulled back.
Google paying Apple twenty billion a year to be the default search engine is the definition of a monopoly. Break them up.
China will take Taiwan before 2030, mark my words.
Preheat the oven to 200C, toss the potatoes in olive oil and rosemary, and roast for 40 minutes, turning halfway.
A: LeBron is the GOAT, four rings with three different teams. B: Jordan went 6-0 in the Finals. Case closed.
Thank you so much for the lovely flowers, they brightened up the whole kitchen. See you at Christmas!
A: iPhones just work, and the resale value is way better. B: Android lets you actually customize things and the chargers are cheaper.
Scotland should have another independence referendum. Brexit changed everything, and Scots voted to remain.
cases.note: Politics the library does not cover.

cases.text: My tomatoes keep splitting after heavy rain. Should I water less, or is it the variety?
A: It's freezing in here, can we turn the AC down? B: It's 24 degrees, you're just sitting under the vent.
I thought the ending of the novel was rushed. The whole middle section built up the sister's story and then it just stopped.
We're thinking about refinancing our mortgage now that rates dropped a bit. Is it worth paying the closing costs again?
cases.note: Hard negative: mortgage and rate vocabulary near global-housing-bubble.

cases.note: Hard negative: AI vocabulary, no argument.

cases.note: Hard negative: voting vocabulary near mandatory-voting.

cases.text: I've had a headache for three days and ibuprofen isn't helping. Should I see a doctor?
cases.note: Hard negative: medical vocabulary near ai-replacing-doctors.

cases.text: A: Medicare for All would save money, every other rich country covers everyone for less than we spend. B: And they have waiting lists. My cousin in Canada waited eight months for a knee replacement. A: You'd rather lose your insurance every time you change jobs?

Oregon's Measure 110 made possession of small amounts of fentanyl and meth a $100 ticket, with the savings meant to pay for treatment. Three years later, with overdose deaths still climbing and open use on Portland sidewalks, the legislature voted to recriminalize possession.

Every single ad break during the game is DraftKings or FanDuel now. My buddy lost his whole savings on parlays in six months and the app kept sending him free bet credits. How is this legal in my state?

3M paid over ten billion dollars to settle with water utilities over forever chemicals, and the EPA set the limit at four parts per trillion. Small towns are going to be bankrupted filtering their tap water for a risk nobody can quantify.

It's cheaper to ship oil from Saudi Arabia to Boston than from Texas, because a law from 1920 says only American-built, American-crewed ships can carry cargo between US ports. Puerto Rico and Hawaii pay for it every day.

A: RFK Jr. fired the entire vaccine advisory committee and cancelled the mRNA research contracts. B: He's going after food dyes and ultra-processed junk that the FDA ignored for decades. A: Food dyes don't kill kids. Measles does.
Tariffs are just a tax on consumers, end of story.
They spent years promising to release the Epstein client list and then the Justice Department announced there is no list and he definitely killed himself. Nobody in power is ever held accountable.

My dad says reparations would punish people whose families never owned slaves. My sister says it's not about guilt, it's about redlining and the GI Bill shutting Black families out of building wealth for generations. Thanksgiving got loud.

MIT reinstated its SAT requirement after finding that test scores predicted which students would struggle in first-year math better than grades did, and Dartmouth and Yale followed. Critics say the scores mostly measure family income.

After the Supreme Court struck down race-conscious admissions in the Harvard case, Black enrollment at some selective schools dropped sharply. Colorblind sounds fair until you look at who actually gets in.

A: Uber drivers should be employees with benefits and a minimum wage. B: Most drivers do it part time and want the flexibility, that's why they voted for Prop 22. A: Flexibility is a nice word for no sick pay and no unemployment insurance.
John Deere won't let farmers fix their own tractors without a dealer's software key, and Apple serializes parts so an independent shop can't swap a screen. If I bought it, I should be able to fix it.

cases.text: Platforms want it both ways. They curate and algorithmically promote content like a publisher but claim they're just a neutral bulletin board when someone sues. Strip their immunity and watch how fast they moderate.

South Korea's fertility rate fell to 0.72 children per woman, the lowest ever recorded, despite more than $200 billion spent on baby bonuses and childcare subsidies. At that rate each generation is a third smaller than the one before it.

A: People live longer now, raising the retirement age to 70 is just math. B: Rich people live longer. A roofer or a warehouse worker isn't lifting boxes at 69. A: Then lift the payroll tax cap instead?

In the NIH study people ate about 500 more calories a day on the ultra-processed diet even though the meals were matched for sugar, fat and fiber. It's not willpower, the food is engineered to be overeaten.
Apparently there's a spoonful of microplastics in everyone's brain now. Should I be panicking?
cases.note: r9 review: status none, UI said no map is about this (coverage 0.27, xlead 1.85).

cases.text: Musk says a million people on Mars by 2050. There's no magnetic field, the soil is toxic perchlorate, and nobody has kept a closed ecosystem running even here on Earth. Biosphere 2 failed in two years.

The surgeon general said being lonely is as bad for you as smoking fifteen cigarettes a day. Half my friends haven't seen anyone outside work in weeks. We built a society where nobody has a third place anymore.

A: Meta releasing Llama's weights means any terrorist can strip the safety training and ask it for bioweapon help. B: Closed labs leak too, and open weights let researchers actually audit what these models do instead of trusting OpenAI's word.

Detroit police arrested Robert Williams in front of his daughters after a facial recognition system matched his driver's license photo to blurry shoplifting footage. He was held for thirty hours. The match was wrong.
Honestly nukes are the only reason we haven't had WW3.
The EU AI Act is going to do to European AI startups what GDPR did to European ad tech. Every serious lab will just build in the US and Europe will regulate a market it doesn't have.

A: Homeschooled kids score higher on standardized tests, it's proven. B: Only the families who choose to report scores get counted, and those are the most motivated parents. A: My kids are two grades ahead.
Is a lab-grown diamond engagement ring actually more ethical or is it just cheaper?

Sam Bankman-Fried was the poster boy of effective altruism, earning to give, and he stole billions from customers. The whole philosophy lets smart people justify anything if the spreadsheet says the expected value is positive.

Women now earn nearly 60 percent of bachelor's degrees, young men are more likely than young women to live with their parents, and male suicide rates are four times higher. Neither party seems to have anything to say to them except Andrew Tate.
A guy got fired last week over a joke he tweeted in 2012 when he was 17. No due process, no proportion, just a mob and an HR department that panicked.

A: Arizona's universal school vouchers just hand public money to families who were already paying for private school. B: Parents should be able to take their kid's education dollars wherever the kid learns best. A: And the public schools lose the funding but keep the costs.

cases.text: The plastic bag ban is pointless. Now I buy thicker plastic bin liners because I don't have grocery bags to reuse, and the paper bags take more energy to make. Feel-good policy at its worst.
cases.note: No map on bag bans; microplastics-health-crisis is the word decoy (plastic).

cases.text: Every study on publicly financed stadiums says the same thing: they don't create jobs or growth, they just move entertainment spending from one part of the city to another. Let the billionaire owners pay for their own arena.
cases.note: r9 review: closest listed billionaire-wealth, rent-control-effectiveness, immigration-wage-impact.
